title: Harmonize backpressure model between continuous batcher and KV cache lifecycle
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Summary: Reduce tail latency variance and simplify operational surface by unifying the backpressure/credit model used by continuous batching with the KV cache lifecycle (eviction/warmup/TTL).

Background: Over time the continuous batcher and the KV cache have diverged: the batcher uses a per-lane token/slot accounting scheme while KV cache eviction and warmup were implemented as independent background agents that sometimes fight scheduling decisions. This manifests as periodic latency spikes under load, unpredictable cold-start behavior for long conversations, and complicated operational knobs.

Objective: Implement a single credit-based resource model and coordinator that: (1) arbitrates request admission across batch lanes and KV cache warmup tasks, (2) exposes deterministic backpressure signals to the API/gateway layer, and (3) provides a TTL-aware eviction policy that cooperates with request routing to minimize cold-kv misses for hot prefixes.

Scope (in-sprint):
- Design and implement a lightweight "resource coordinator" module in the runtime that tracks credits for GPU compute slots and KV memory budget.
- Replace per-lane hard timeouts with coordinator-driven admission (credit borrow/repay semantics).
- Move KV warmup into coordinator-controlled background tasks with prioritized warmup for recently admitted requests.
- Implement a new KV eviction controller based on TTL score + recent-access priority that avoids evicting entries that are being warmed.
- Add metrics and tracing (admission_latency_ms, coordinator_credit_usage, kv_warmup_queue_length, eviction_score) and dashboard tiles.
- Add integration tests and end-to-end perf harness scenarios (steady-state 1k rps, sustained burst 10k rps, long-conversation 64k tokens).

Out-of-scope for this ticket: kernel-level GPU scheduling, full rearchitecture of batch lanes to multi-tenant lanes (follow-up ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
- Mean 95th percentile per-token latency improves by at least 15% in the long-conversation benchmark compared to baseline (runtime-1.18 config).
- Cold-kv miss rate for warmup-prioritized prefixes drops >= 40% under burst load.
- New coordinator exposes metrics and no regressions on throughput in steady-state tests.
- Config knobs documented in Console and default conservative values applied.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Chosen model: credit borrowing with decay to be simple to reason about and inexpensive to compute. We considered a hierarchical leaky-bucket but rejected it because the compute overhead and complexity for coordination across shards outweighed benefits.
- KV eviction: TTL+recency score provides predictable behavior; a ML-based eviction policy was scoped out for later experiments.
- Rolling strategy: start with a feature-flagged rollout on dedicated staging pools to verify safety before enabling in host clusters.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for coordinator state machine (credit acquisition/release, edge cases).
- Integration tests that assert no deadlock with simultaneous warmup and admission.
- Synthetic load tests in perf infra with dashboard snapshots for comparison.
- Canary rollout on 5% of Dedicated fleet with synthetic probe traffic and automated rollback on SLA breach.

Monitoring and rollback:
- Dashboard alerts: coordinator_credit_saturation > 80% for > 5m, kv_warmup_backlog > 500, p95_latency_increase > 10% vs baseline.
- Automatic rollback policy: if canary breaches any alert for > 5m, rollback to previous runtime image and disable coordinator.

Implementation notes / tasks:
- Spike week (2d): prototype coordinator proto with in-memory credits. Owner: Liam.
- Core implementation (6d): integrate with batcher admission path and KV agent. Owner: Priya + Samir.
- Metrics and tracing (1d): add OpenTelemetry spans and Prometheus metrics. Owner: Maya.
- Perf runs and dashboard updates (2d): Diego to run and capture baselines.
- Docs + Console knobs (1d): Doc changes and console flagging. Owner: Ken.

Useful links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Coordinator+Backpressure+Design
- Perf dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/runtime/backpressure-2026-march
- Experimental PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1245

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Coordinator becomes single point of contention. Mitigation: provide sharded coordinator instances per-GPU-slice and benchmark contention during spike runs.
- Risk: Unexpected interaction with legacy autoscaler. Mitigation: coordinate with infra on a temporary compatibility layer and run joint canary.
- Risk: Eviction changes increase memory pressure. Mitigation: conservative defaults with tracing and ability to revert eviction controller only.

Next steps: schedule design review with infra and batcher owners (invite: Diego, Samir, Ava Chen, Noah Kim), land prototype branch behind feature flag, and create follow-up ticket for multi-tenant lane changes once metrics are stable.
